label: copy-phase input u fed back at recall step 1-2 with >=3 outputs left
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input is the letter u. That u is the model own output fed back in, i.e. original token 0 or 1 was u. Only fires at recall steps 1-2, so right after DEL (u at position 0) or two steps after (u at position 1). It is strongest when u is the first original token and many outputs remain (long sequences, large to_go). It is weak or silent when L is short (to_go <= 2). It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, on u fed back later in the copy (recall_idx >= 3), or on any other token. Dev F1 0.92, mass recall 0.97.

issues: Every factual claim checks out. In dev, 100% of the activation mass is in the copy phase. All of it is on in_tok=u. recall_idx 1 holds 0.607 of the mass, recall_idx 2 holds 0.392, and recall_idx 3 has 114 steps and 0.001 of the mass. Nothing fires on the original phase or the delimiter. Mass rises with to_go (to_go 6 holds 0.306), and the t=8-10 peak is real.
Test scores reproduce: P 0.916, R 0.917, F1 0.916, mass recall 0.972. Without the to_go term, test F1 is 0.850.

The to_go>=3 cut approximates a graded effect that depends on sequence length, so it is not a sharp boundary. Test false positives (2090) are short sequences (L=5-6) at to_go 3-4 where the feature stays silent. Restricted to L<=6, the predicate's precision is only 0.78. Test misses (2058) are weak activations at to_go=2, about 0.03-0.23 of max, in L=4-5 sequences. Together the misses hold only 2.8% of the mass.
The cut shifts by one step between the two cases. Allowing to_go>=2 at recall_idx 1 but requiring to_go>=3 at recall_idx 2 gives a slightly better test F1 of 0.921 with mass recall 0.991.

Small edge case: when orig(0)=orig(1)=u, the second u (recall_idx 2) fires only 60% of the time. Top examples show it does fire, but more weakly. It covers about 1.4% of activations, so it is negligible.
